label: NYFL potential diamonds
definition: Young, inexpensive players whose 2026 acquisition cost could become a materially better 2027 keeper price. This is an upside screen, not a breakout probability or a redraft ranking.

methodology.formula: 30% 2027 role ceiling + 25% keeper-cost leverage + 20% prospect/dynasty signal + 15% current path to snaps + 10% durability and rosterability
rules: Prefer players likely to cost a Round 10-16 selection or remain available for a Round 16 free-agent keeper price.
Require a plausible route to a starting role or premium fantasy usage by 2027.
Do not treat the score as an injury-free probability or a recommendation to reach above the target range.
Recheck role, health, and ADP before the draft; a rising price can erase the keeper edge.

candidates.keeperThesis: Second-round NFL capital, first-team work, size and red-zone traits create a realistic path to Cleveland's long-term perimeter WR1 role at a near-free keeper cost.
candidates.redraftPath: Can earn immediate perimeter and red-zone work; current price leaves room for the role to grow without forcing him into a weekly lineup.
candidates.risk: Cleveland's passing environment may cap Year 1 production and KC Concepcion could command the higher-volume role.

candidates.keeperThesis: Premium rookie capital and a short-area role give him the cleanest volume path in Cleveland; a Round 10-plus price could become a weekly PPR starter kept well below market.
candidates.redraftPath: Designed touches and slot volume can make him useful before the offense fully develops.
candidates.risk: His draft price is rising and a crowded rookie receiver room could keep the ceiling uneven early.

candidates.keeperThesis: First-round prospect value at a final-round fantasy price creates unusually strong cost leverage if he wins the Jets' long-term slot job.
candidates.redraftPath: May begin behind a veteran, but one role change could unlock immediate slot targets.
candidates.risk: The opening-day role is not secure, so he may require patience or a waiver re-add.

candidates.keeperThesis: A rising rookie with encouraging camp and preseason usage can become a starting-caliber young receiver while still carrying a late-round keeper price.
candidates.redraftPath: Early production and positive role reports give him a faster path to relevance than a typical deep rookie stash.
candidates.risk: The role and health trend must be checked immediately before the draft; preseason momentum can be fragile.

candidates.keeperThesis: Third-round NFL capital, size and a possible red-zone role next to Zay Flowers give him a low-cost route to becoming Baltimore's long-term No. 2 receiver.
candidates.redraftPath: A final-round selection can be held through the first role tests without sacrificing meaningful draft capital.
candidates.risk: Baltimore can remain run-heavy and veteran competition may delay consistent routes.

candidates.keeperThesis: A young receiver with an attainable starting role and evidence of NFL production can turn a cheap pick into a stable future starter if Carolina's passing game develops.
candidates.redraftPath: He has a clearer immediate route to weekly snaps than many players drafted in the same range.
candidates.risk: His ceiling depends on target quality and whether Carolina adds or elevates another receiver.

candidates.keeperThesis: Young tight ends often gain value after their rookie acclimation period; a late price preserves the chance to keep a future every-down receiving tight end before the market reprices him.
candidates.redraftPath: A developmental bench slot with touchdown and route-growth upside rather than an immediate weekly starter.
candidates.risk: Tight-end breakouts can take multiple seasons and the 2026 target floor may be low.

candidates.keeperThesis: A cheap rookie running back attached to an unsettled depth chart can gain keeper value quickly with one role change, even if his immediate touch projection is modest.
candidates.redraftPath: Bench stash and contingency back whose value rises sharply with depth-chart movement.
candidates.risk: He may remain a limited committee player and running-back role value can disappear quickly.

candidates.keeperThesis: A near-free young receiver can become a valuable keeper if he claims a durable outside role; the acquisition cost makes the miss inexpensive.
candidates.redraftPath: Final-round role bet whose early route participation should decide whether to hold or churn the spot.
candidates.risk: The path to meaningful targets is less proven than the higher-scored candidates.

candidates.keeperThesis: The Round 16/free-agent keeper mechanism makes a young receiver with a plausible role spike worth monitoring even when his median outcome is a roster churn.
candidates.redraftPath: Use the final pick or early waivers only if the route share and depth-chart evidence remain positive.
candidates.risk: Low draft capital and uncertain target priority create a wide miss rate.

candidates.keeperThesis: If he is undrafted, the NYFL free-agent rule can lock in a Round 16 keeper price for a talented young receiver whose value could rebound after recovery.
candidates.redraftPath: IR-only stash; do not spend a normal bench spot while he is unavailable.
candidates.risk: Season-ending injury and uncertain recovery make this a long-horizon option, not a 2026 production bet.
